name: Gel Transfusor
description: When any unit dies, their [pyregel] is spread among enemy units.
lore: There are rumors amongst the whelps that if they don't get their numbers up, Lady Gilda will shoot Pyregel in their veins to 'put a little fire' in them.

name: Imp-cicle
description: At start of turn, add a random [imp] unit to hand.
lore: When Seraph shattered our Hell Pyre and Hell froze over, many unsuspecting imps were caught in the ice. Taken aboard the Boneshaker, the Pyre shard slowly melts them free.

name: Attuned Whetstone
description: On [deployphase], draw an Equipment card from your deck. Reduce its cost to 0[ember].
lore: As I sharpened the blades of clan soldiers, I wondered if I would ever see them again. Quartz absorbs the emotions around it and soon my whetstone absorbed my wishes for the safety of my friends.

name: Shardsoul
description: +[effect0.power][ember] per turn. +[effect1.power][deploymentember]. +[effect2.power][capacity] on each floor. Draw +[effect3.power] each turn.
lore: I have seen the Exiles sacrifice themselves and witnessed the fate of Heaven and Hell shaped by these shards. Now that they lie within reach of others, I fear the consequences they may bring.The Historian

name: Carriage Jack
description: When you play a Room card, apply +[effect0.power][capacity] on the floor.
lore: The original Boneshaker used to be a multi-car train. It was only when the fighting began that the line of carriages were abandoned in favor of a single, tall carriage, which made defending the Pyre an easier task. The single car design has remained the standard, and has since been inherited by the Skull Crusher.

name: Lightstone Casing
description: Spells get an extra upgrade slot.
lore: After the Pyrestone brace proved to be wildly successful, Seraph stole my design and created a similar device to infuse the stones with Light instead. As is his way, he created a housing much more ostentatious than the simple one I created for Hell.

name: Steel Stockpile
description: Conserve up to [effect0.power] [forgepoints] between battles.
lore: A vast physical reserve of iron and steel was established in Hell, long before the fighting began. The reserve was indespensible for the construction of the Covenant Outpost and the Skull Crusher, and somehow there is still a portion left untouched.

name: Token of a Traitor
description: Playing a spell deals [effect0.power] damage to a random enemy unit on that floor.
lore: When the Covenant was formed, Seraph made a diplomatic offering to the Titan at my suggestion. It should have been telling that the pearl immediately turned black when the Traitor touched it.

name: Astrologer's Orrery
description: The first time each turn it becomes [full] gain [effect0.power][ember].
lore: Hmm... I see a malicious moon is coming in your star chart. A few gold coins and I might see how you can avoid this calamity. Astrologer for the Luna Coven

name: Traitor's Quill
description: When a card with [consume] is played, deal [effect0.power] damage to the front enemy unit.
lore: Seraph was not always the Traitor he is today, hellbent on the unification of Heaven and Hell for our mutual survival. He was the main reason the Covenant was pursued to begin with. I suppose his need for control finally got the better of him...

name: Bone Dog's Pendant
description: The first time the Pyre reaches [effect0.secondarypower] health, restore the Pyre to [effect0.power]% health. This can only trigger once.
lore: Although I was not able to give much to this pup, I tried to give him love. I hope whenever he hears the clink of his collar's tag, he'll be reminded of all the fun we had.

name: Teeth of Gold
description: Deal [effect0.power] [piercing] damage to the lowest health enemy unit when a unit is [eaten].
lore: On the rare occasion that a member of the Shroud has lost their teeth, sharp dentures are created from Crucible gems. Due to their high value, this has led to many Umbra intentionally removing their teeth.

name: Blood of the Apex
description: Permanently add +[effect0.trigger0.effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] to a unit's Equipment on [slay].
lore: Feed me, hissed the sword. For the blade craved blood and would not be sated until its steel was fed.

name: Scorching Restraints
description: Friendly units enter with [rage] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: For the Hellhorned that are considered too violent by their own clan's standards, imprisonment is a cruel affair. Subjected to rot in chains sunk directly into the bubbling lava below, the prisoners are burned by the molten steel that binds them... and the scorching heat only enrages them further.

name: Silver Draw
description: Draw +[effect0.power] each turn.

name: Advanced Growth
description: When an equipped unit dies, permanently add +[effect0.trigger0.effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] to their Equipment.
lore: This bottle certainly gives off mixed messages. Between the skull and the note with the instructions 'Eat Me,' it's unclear what you're supposed to do.

name: Heph's Blueprints
description: When you [forge] an equipment, apply +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and [armor] [effect0.upgrade.status0.power] for each [forgepoint] spent.
lore: I am consistently amazed by my daughter's ingenuity. The additions she has made to the Skull Crusher build upon my own designs in ways I never thought to attempt. Herzal, My Workshop, My Life

name: Refined Void
description: Friendly units enter with [lifesteal] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: While the Umbra doesn't appear to become inebriated like other denizens of Hell, they've still taken to processing Void Shards into a liquid that mildly dulls the senses. When the Shroud consumes it, the drink makes them somewhat less unpleasant in my dealings with them.

name: Canio
description: When you [annihilate] a card outside of combat, gain [effect0.power][coin].
lore: Laugh, Clown at your broken love! Laugh at the grief that poisons your heart!

name: Sketches of Salvation
description: On the turn after [deployphase], summon a random unit from your deck on each floor.
lore: There was little time to act after Seraph's invasion, but there was just enough for me to design a way to protect what would remain of the Pyre after its inevitable destruction.

name: Combustible Wax
description: When a friendly unit gains [burnout], it gains +[effect0.status0.power] stacks.
lore: Created for more urgent circumstances, the Wickless granted me this bomb for an emergency supply of wax on detonation. Having no need for it, I ended up giving it to the Waxers to increase their chances of survival.

name: Shaleshell
description: After using an ability, friendly units gain [armor] [effect0.power].
lore: Fhyra wore such a shield during the battle of the First Pyre. Although she was consumed by her own flames, this part of her armor was somehow spared.

name: Priory's Cloak
description: When a friendly unit is healed, deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to the amount healed.
lore: A cloak gifted to me from a Channeler of the Edge Priory. It still contains some residual energy from its owner, allowing anyone who wears it to heal their wounds more effectively. Though this energy is not without side effects...

name: Departure Manifest
description: Non-banner units have [deployable].
lore: All the clans of Hell knew one thing to be true: that victory flew on the wings of careful planning. Whenever armies set out to battle, their ranks and schedules were recorded with precision in the train's manifest.

name: Pact of the First Armageddon
description: Drafts only offer selections from your allied clan.
lore: For years I have searched for this reliquary from the days of the First Armageddon, the terrible war that brought Angels and Demons together, only to find the chest sealed. The scripture etched along the sides speaks of a binding contract and a great boon for those who open the lock. Now I must wait for a warrior to try their hand instead.The Historian

name: Votive Key
description: Apply [endless] to the first friendly unit played each turn.
lore: Keys to Votive Houses have secretly circulated in Waxer communities for eons, with new copies being made all the time to evade detection of the original thief. Having come across a couple in my travels, I've kept them for myself in case the need for one arises.

name: The Clepsydranium
description: Friendly units gain [conduit] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power] on [slay].
lore: A 'water clock' filled with ink instead of water. The ink inside sloshes as if it had a mind of its own.

name: Everchurning Soil
description: Draw +1 each turn per [effect0.power] cards in your Deck.
lore: On the eve of the Creation Elm's destruction, the shroomfolk drink a mixture of soil taken from around the Fatal Elm mixed with water to remind themselves of what they have lost.

name: Razorthin Crescent
description: [mageblade] adds an additional <nobr>+[effect0.power][attack]</nobr> per stack.
lore: A blade carved from the moon itself and so thin that it cannot be seen, apart from when it gleams in the moonlight.

name: Large Mystery Box
description: Add a random card to your hand each turn.
lore: What's inside?

name: Lifemother's Seed
description: At the end of combat, create a permanent copy of a random non-champion card in your deck.
lore: Interesting, indeed, and not uncharacteristic of the Lifemother. This has not been the first time a fragment of Her magic has bloomed from beneath marbled floors. Nor, I fear, will it be the last.The Historian

name: Channelheart
description: Sting spells get +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage] [magicpower].
lore: Before the Edge Priory became the reclusive group they are now, they would channel their energy into steel lockets that could be worn by their Awoken Hollow protectors, allowing the Hollows to gain more strength at the cost of their longevity.

name: Shattered Halo
description: Clan card drafts only offer rares.
lore: A general of heaven long forgotten once possessed this halo, up until their sudden defeat they were said to have uncommonly good luck.

name: Queen's Tail
description: When you summon your first [imp] unit each turn, gain [effect0.power][ember] and draw [effect0.power].
lore: From what I can gather, the Queen had the only full-grown Demon tail in existence. Yet, in the visions I've spent with her, this tail has been replaced by her Shardsoul tail. Did this replacement grant the Hellhorned the ability to cycle, making them immortal? It's as if a large shadow looms over any memory I should have of these Exiles...

name: Collection of Tails
description: [rage] does not decay on friendly units.
lore: An imp officially matures into a demon when their tail falls off and they learn to stand on their own feet, but this evolution only seems to enrage the demon further. I don't like the sight of the disembodied tails, but keeping them is necessary.

name: Moonstone
description: At end of turn, if it is [full], spells in hand gain +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage] [magicpower].
lore: Take this stone, marked by Ekka's blessing, and place it outside when the moon is full. You will always have a piece of the moon's protection with you wherever you go. The Ritual Tome

name: Ember Foundry Crucible
description: [smelt] grants an additional +[effect0.power][ember].
lore: Instead of smelting metal, the Ember Foundry smelted calcified embers, excavated by the Umbra Shroud. These dormant embers could be reinvigorated through many means, but the most efficient method was to use the heat of a Pyre Heart itself.

name: Lost Luggage
description: On the turn after [deployphase], draw until you have [effect0.power] cards.
lore: Contrary to common belief, demons do not travel light. Supposedly, the souls of Heaven and Hell require less worldly attachments than the Humans they consider to be so lowly, but I can tell you that is absolutely untrue. I once saw a Hellhorned Demon bring aboard six bursting suitcases. When I asked if all of it was needed, the Demon only glared and growled. Only then, have I truly known fear.

name: Evolutionary Instinct
description: When a unit has a third unique status effect applied to it, [propagate] [effect0.effect0.power].
lore: The Fatal Elm is the source of life and from its branches new plants are born.

name: Lifemother's Remnant
description: Create a permanent copy of the first non-champion card played each turn.
lore: There are countless records of Angels and Demons claiming they heard whispers from the Lifemother from beneath the roots and that She cries from her prison. I've searched for traces of Her power but have yet to find proof. That is, until today.The Historian

name: Hidden Coffers
description: Increase max [dragonshoardicon] by [effect0.power].
lore: You can tell a lot from a dragon's treasure chest. An empty trove reveals an empty mind. The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #14

name: Spiritbreaker's Charge
description: After using an ability, friendly units gain +[effect0.power][attack].
lore: A motivational tool used on dragons whose quarterly returns are deemed unacceptable.

name: Gnarled Root
description: Friendly units get +[effect0.power][attack] per stack of [spikes].
lore: The roots of the Wildwood spread farther than just their own Ring, but the farther they travel from the center of the wood, the more likely they are to wither and die.

name: Herzal's Anvil
description: When you [forge], gain +[effect0.power] [forgepoint].
lore: After completing the Rail, Herzal destroyed his anvil as a symbol that his life's work was complete. When he founded the Railforged clan, he forged a new one more durable than even his first anvil to symbolize the beginning of a new chapter in his life.

name: Divine Shard
description: Your Pyre gets [effect0.power][health].
lore: Heaven and Hell thought that the Last Divinity would be the last of the Titans... hence the name they called it. They were, unfortunately, quite wrong.

name: Base Charge
description: At the start of battle, add [effect0.power][corrupt] to each floor.
lore: The carving of stoneform is a long and tedious process, not entirely suitable for capturing fleeting thought. Some Wurmkin have created small Echo necklaces to preserve their knowledge on the fly, storing their observations directly onto the small crystal. Still, most of the clan finds the practice irreverent.

name: Sizzling Firecracker
description: Spells gain +[effect0.power] damage for each upgrade on their card.
lore: Although this product sounds cute, it's enough to break into any vault along the Rail without destroying the gold inside.

name: Triboulet
description: Friendly units gain +[effect0.power][health] for each rare card in your deck.
lore: Jesters do oft prove prophets.

name: Taskmaster's Lash
description: When you damage your own unit, reduce [cooldown] by [effect0.powerabs].
lore: I love my adorable golden crumpet but when she snaps her whip she is terrifying! Lord Fenix

name: Breath of Heaven
description: [advance] the back enemy unit when it enters your train.
lore: When Angels and Demons were created, they were given the Breath of Life. Over time, Seraph manipulated this innate ability in all beings so that it became a powerful force that knocks an enemy back.

name: Petrified Crucible
description: [spikes] deal +[effect0.power] damage per stack.
lore: A tool made of petrified Wildwood bark, used to heat ores into something stronger. Used by the Edge Priory to create armor for their Hollows, a process that astounds me still.

name: Skysong Trumpet
description: Summoning a Hymnist applies [valor] [effect0.status0.power] to friendly units.
lore: Taken from a fallen guard of Heaven's Maw, the Deathmetal Hymnist is now learning to play this rockin' horn.

name: Void Fragment
description: At the end of the entire battle, purge a card.
lore: The tiny vortex confined within this orb is indistinguishable from the ones scattered across Heaven and Hell. These rifts were long thought to be natural phenomena, pockets of space that opened up into the Void. Yet the orb's existence implies that they can be created. If so, then perhaps the great rift in Heaven was no accident, but of a similar hand at work.

name: Dante's Candelabra
description: The Pyre gains [titanskin] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: Dante's candles burn as hot as the Pyre itself, yet his candelabra makes the heat somehow bearable. Always been a man of many mysteries.

name: Exploding Candle
description: Deal [effect0.power] damage to enemy units when a [burnout] unit dies.
lore: When Flicker decided to help me unite the Ring and build the Rail, he lit a ceremonial candle to commemorate the event. Appropriately, the current state of the candle reflects the state of the Covenant it was created to represent.

name: Hellfire Bellows
description: When a unit gains [pyregel], it gains +[effect0.status0.power] stacks.
lore: A mainstay tool used by the Pyreborne smelters. These bellows can withstand the hottest fires.

name: Tuning Gear
description: Friendly units enter with [burst] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: Beneath their plating, stewards are an amalgamation of gears and conduits, fueled by the Pyre's flame. They are almost entirely machine, yet any who have worked alongside them say that the spark within them acts with a faint will of its own.

name: Hair of the Hybrid
description: Equipping a friendly unit under half health applies [armor] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power], otherwise it applies [rage] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status1.power].
lore: When hair strands are powdered, mixed, and then ingested, the resulting mixture has shown promise in energizing my subjects. from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Commemorative Spike
description: On the turn after [deployphase], summon a Morsel Miner on each floor.
lore: Once the Rail was complete, I returned to the Crucible to enlist the Shroud's help to create the Boneshaker. When the last bolt was punched into the train, they drove one last spike into the Rail to memorialize the train's departure.

name: Encased Ember
description: Gain [effect0.power][ember] when a [tomb] unit dies.
lore: It seems that throughout the existence of the Waxen Arches, everything has fallen victim to wax encasement. Not even the Ember of the Pyre has been spared, though I've collected any I've seen trapped to free them again later.

name: Inga's Beaker
description: Increase the number of choices when using [mix] by [effect0.power].
lore: A forgotten piece of equipment collecting dust in the corner of Dr. Orechi's lab. Once used by a renowned researcher not soon forgotten, the unknown liquid inside still bubbles from time to time.

name: Wolo's Bloodletter
description: Friendly units get +[effect1.power][attack]. At end of combat, deal [effect0.power] damage to friendly units.
lore: Whoever once owned this must have had an incredible pain tolerance, as wearing it would feel like enduring countless papercuts at every moment.

name: Titan's Claws
description: At end of turn, [freeze] cards are reduced to [effect0.power][ember] until played or discarded.
lore: The sharp claws of the Titan. They were lodged into the stone as the Titan tried to escape prison we'd built for it. Now, they serve as a reminder of the strength we locked away.

name: Vola's Tuning Fork
description: Starter cards cost -[effect0.upgrade.costreduction][ember].
lore: Her celestial song was said to be sweet enough to bring peace to a battlefield. Some still hold out hope that she will one day return.

name: Shroomponics
description: At start of turn, friendly units [propagate] [effect0.power].
lore: When their forest was threatened by the Great Decay, the shroomfolk made this device to carry their young and keep them safe.

name: Volatile Gauge
description: When you draw any non-Champion card, its cost is randomized between 0[ember] and 3[ember]. Draw +[effect1.power] each turn.
lore: One of the first instruments I developed for the Boneshaker. Regrettably, it's not very accurate and delivers entirely random heat output from the furnace.

name: Resonant Shard
description: [rage] adds an additional <nobr>+[effect0.power][attack]</nobr> per stack.
lore: I modified the Pyre so that the sound it makes when it is threatened can no longer be heard by any creature, in Heaven or in Hell. However, an unintended consequence has been observed: distant Pyre shards will resonate with the same frequency and vibrate wildly, sometimes even shattering.

name: Life Insurer
description: Friendly units gain [armor] [effect0.power] on reviving with [undying].
lore: My experiments are not only of the scientific sort. I also enjoy dabbling in more fashionable pursuits. This piece from my fall line is functional and stylish! from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Sapsuckling Spring
description: [shroom] units apply [decay] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power] to enemy units on [summon].
lore: When the moons reach the rotten quadrant in the sky, the shroomfolk celebrate by drinking distilled sap from the trees.

name: Hell's Flame
description: +[effect0.power][ember] per turn. +[effect3.power][deploymentember]. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].
lore: When Fel left to join her cause, she left me with remaining Embers of the Pyre. She could have been killed for this, but she gave them anyway. That's all I have to say about Fel.

name: The Dragonstone
description: Gain [effect0.power][dragonshoardicon] on the first turn of battle.
lore: Said to have been made from a scale from Fhyra herself, the Dragonstone brings prosperity to whichever dragon possesses it. If said dragon loses the stone, however, they face destitution.

name: Mask of Penumbra
description: When you play your first [snack] unit each turn, draw [effect0.power].
lore: A discarded mask of the shadow known as Penumbra. I've encountered several of these throughout the mines. The shadow seems to outgrow them quickly.

name: Perkeo
description: At the start of battle, gain a Calcified Ember that converts to Excavated Ember after not playing it once.
lore: Why so serious?

name: Prismatic Dragonscale
description: At the end of battle, gain [effect0.power][dragonshoardicon] if your Pyre took no damage.
lore: Never trust hard-earned riches, it's the easy coin that will get you by. The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #37

name: Celestial Sails
description: On [deployphase], draw a non-damage spell from your deck. It costs -[effect0.upgrade.costreduction][ember].
lore: After the Fall, I searched the wreckage of our moon and found this sail. I remembered how the flightless fae used to play with these in the wind. Ardania the Forbidden

name: Hell's Flame
description: +[effect0.power][ember] per turn. +[effect3.power][deploymentember]. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].
lore: When Fel left to join her cause, she left me with remaining Embers of the Pyre. She could have been killed for this, but she gave them anyway. That's all I have to say about Fel.

name: Kingdom's Tears
description: Increases healing from spells by [effect0.power].
lore: When the Titans destroyed our home, they shattered our moon into tiny fragments. This vial contains the last of our home. Arduhn, twin brother of Lady Ekka

name: Sacrificial Kris
description: Apply [pyregel] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power] to enemy units when a Whelp dies.
lore: The temple priests carry a dagger they only use for one specific ritual: the sacrifice of unprofitable dragons to the great Fhyra.

name: Pressurized Boiler
description: The Pyre gains [burst] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: The Pyre may be, as far as we know, a near infinite heat source, but the boilers still require refueling. Fortunately, working fluid from the Stygian Sea is always in abundant supply, and the engineers have cleverly built enough storage to fuel long trips along the rail without needing to refuel.

name: World-ending Strain
description: When a unit dies to [decay], their [decay] is spread among enemy units.
lore: We locked the Great Decay away and buried it beneath the roots of what was once the Creation Elm. May it never open or we are all doomed. The Archives of the Great Decay

name: Looming Darkshard
description: When you draw a Blight or Scourge, gain 1[ember] and draw a non-Blight or non-Scourge card.
lore: Sometimes a curse can be a blessing in disguise. While Hell is filled with so many opportunities for pain, they often make a demon stronger.

name: Consumed Crown
description: Friendly units gain +[effect0.power][attack] on [slay].
lore: When a Hellhorned defeats another in battle, they will break off the loser's horns and add it to their collection, forming them into a crown. I've learned the hard way that asking to wear another's crown is considered incredibly rude.

name: Icicle Fracture
description: At end of turn, apply [freeze] to a random card in your hand.
lore: Ice created from the water of the Styx Sea melts at much higher temperatures than other ice I've found throughout Hell. Any icicles that form on the Boneshaker while in this Ring will not thaw entirely from the train's residual heat, and will become potential hazards for negligent bystanders.

name: Sharpened Teeth
description: Dragons and Whelps gain +[effect0.power][attack].
lore: When a dragon loses their teeth from eating too much sweetened gold, such sharp dentures must be worn. They have become such a fashion statement among the elite Pyreborne.

name: Chain of Gems
description: Apply [damageshield] [effect0.status0.power] to the first friendly unit summoned each turn.
lore: I constructed this as a gift to Penumbra for his help with the Covenant. The necklace is made out of the finest gems found in the Crucible. For whatever reason, Penumbra tossed it aside, perhaps considering it too gaudy.

name: Dante's Footstool
description: On [deployphase], draw a Room card from your deck. Reduce its cost to 0[ember].
lore: A strange object that somehow always seems to appear in a room before Dante himself.

name: Frenzystesia
description: The first time each turn a friendly unit is equipped, gain [effect0.power][ember].
lore: The doctor's latest experiment has made all the subjects frenzy. And made me have a migraine. Hugo, assistant to Dr. Orechi

name: Winged Technology
description: [snack] units enter with [damageshield] [effect0.upgrade.status0.power].
lore: For all their faults and treacherous tendencies, the Winged excel at developing new technology. Lucky for us, Antumbra Morsels were able to steal some of it for our collective benefit.

name: Gros Michel
description: Non-champion friendly units gain +[effect0.power][attack]. At the end of combat on all floors, [effect1.power]% chance for this artifact to be destroyed.
lore: Peel my wrath!

name: Sigiled Seaweed
description: Apply [mute] [effect0.effect0.status0.power] when an enemy unit enters your train.
lore: The seaweed of the Sea is known to be very resistant to breaking. The addition of Stygian sigils make breaking it impossible, despite all my efforts.

name: Fossilized Fangs
description: [feed] triggers an additional time.
lore: There are more victims in mine collapses than I would've first thought. Many Umbra have fallen victim to these accidents and while they fade back into the shadow, their teeth remain.

name: Fae's Nook
description: Fae gain [conduit] [effect0.effect1.status0.power] and +[effect0.effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] on [mooncycle].
lore: Psst! Can you pass me some stardust treats? We're running low in here!

name: Crystallized Wing
description: [x] Cost cards and cards that cost [effect0.power][ember] or more have [permafrost].
lore: Among Heaven's relics lies a wing encased within crystal. Its resemblance to an angel's wing is only in shape, for it bears no feathers. Some archivists dismissed it as a curiosity; others wondered if it marked a lineage long sundered from Heaven.

name: Dun Echo
description: One additional card in each draft pack will be [infused].
lore: An Echo with no knowledge is just another piece of rock. At least, that's what the Wurmkin would have you believe. The way they toss around empty Echoes, their knowledge retrieved, makes me wonder if their so-called reverence for knowledge has been emphasized for their own egos.

name: Mine Jacks
description: +[effect0.power][capacity] on the middle floor.
lore: These immense jacks are used to prevent the Crucible from collapsing. At the speed the Umbra seems to be mining it, I'm not sure these jacks will help it.

name: Flicker's Liquor
description: After [deployphase], when you play a unit a random card in hand is reduced to 0[ember] until played or discarded.
lore: Flicker has been known to imbibe on occasion, and when he can't find me to drink with him, he'll corner unlucky Waxers who quickly succumb to its effects.

name: Chain of the Valkyrie
description: When you equip an Angel, apply [valor] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power], [rage] [effect0.trigger0.effect1.status0.power], and [regen] [effect0.trigger0.effect2.status0.power].
lore: The iron chain of an Empyrial Palace guard, taken in battle and now used by the Banished.

name: Versatile Emberstaff
description: When you play three different kinds of cards in a turn, draw [effect0.power] and gain [effect0.secondarypower][ember].
lore: To guide Dante in his descent through Hell, Beatrice gifted him a staff infused by her angelic hands to guide him.

name: Deepwood Oil
description: When you equip a friendly unit, apply [armor] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power].
lore: Long ago, young demons ventured into the Wild Woods and dipped their blades in the forest rivers. Their reward for their bravery was a blade that would never break.

name: Cuttlebeard
description: When a unit gains [frostbite], it gains +[effect0.status0.power] stacks. [frostbite] does not decay.
lore: It seems that the energy of the Cuttlehex and the Molluscmages does not die with them, but continues to surge through their beards so long as they are kept intact. I've kept some of the beards with me. They've been quite useful, but the tentacles make me a tad squeamish.

name: Attuned Manacles
description: The first time you summon a Whelp each turn, reduce the [cooldown] of friendly units on all floors by [effect0.power].
lore: For the Pyreborne who desire to lead lives governed by love and joy instead of gold, their fate lies in imprisonment. They are left to tend to Fhyra's temple and never seen again.

name: Sparkflint Catalyst
description: When a unit without [pyregel] gains [pyregel], it gains +[effect0.status0.power] stacks.
lore: A small but mighty weapon that might just give a dragon enough time to escape.

name: Wing Clippings
description: Spell cards with [consume] have a [effect0.power]% chance to be discarded instead.
lore: Clipped Wings are discarded after removal to suppress any hope of the victim's redemption. However, I was able to smuggle some out of Heaven disguised as Waxer rags.

name: Titan's Edict
description: [valor] grants an additional +[effect0.power] [armor] per stack.
lore: A slab of stone bearing a language long forgotten. The claw marks, however, seem much newer than the age of the stone would grant.

name: Emblem of the Exiles
description: At start of turn, the front friendly unit on each floor gains +[effect0.upgrade.bonushp][health].
lore: Wyldenten speaks in these visions of the Exiles' purpose to forestall the Divinities desertion and avoid Armageddon. This history has been lost to time, it seems, as we've only created this new destruction ourselves.

name: Crown of the Eternal
description: At start of turn, fully heal Champions.
lore: The queen who once wore this crown is long gone but her magic still rests within its glittering gems.

name: Rootsplit Mask
description: Apply [rooted] to enemy units when they enter the floor below the Pyre Room.
lore: Breaking through their armor is considered a rite of passage for the Awoken, marking their shift from Hollow to Animus. This old armor breaks under the weight of new vines making up the Animus.

name: Leaky Pen
description: [effect0.power][ember] per turn. Draw [effect1.power] additional cards per turn.
lore: An antique pen whose owner must have held the pen too tight, for it now leaks ink everywhere.

name: Winged Steel
description: After [deployphase], when you play your third card of the turn, draw [effect0.power].
lore: The Winged crafted a solid piece of steel to show me the creation process. The runes they placed on it made sure I could not melt it down again for my own use.

name: Sinner's Salve
description: Blights and Scourges cost 0[ember].
lore: Collaboration between the Rings of Hell was rare, but the few that did occur produced wondrous results. Water from the Stygian Sea blessed by the Channelers of the Wildwood created a solution capable of soothing the pains of Heaven's wretched sinner contraptions. However, this was used only a handful of times. Those contraptions rarely had survivors...

name: Encased Divinity
description: At the start of battle, the top floor gains [effect0.power][corrupt] that cannot be removed.
lore: Echoes are the essence of Divinity. There is no recorded history of this, and, frankly, anyone claiming this fact would be considered mad. But given my recent... revelations... I can say without a doubt that their origin is Divine.

name: Abyssal Prism
description: The first time each turn you target a friendly unit with a spell, non-move effects also hit all other friendly units on the floor.
lore: When I look into the Pyre, I see the monster I have become. Perhaps, if I was to remove my Titanhood from my body, this nightmare might end.

name: Captain's Halo
description: At start of turn, the front friendly unit on each floor gains [valor] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.upgrade.charactertrigger0.effect0.status0.power].
lore: While the aristocrats of the Empyrial Palace inherit their crowns, within the ranks of the Banished they are earned.

name: Hope for Peace
description: Spells and Equipment with [annihilate] have [consume] instead.
lore: As elusive as their name, these bright flowers bloom briefly in the cracked soil of the Scorched Plains, quickly smothered by the harsh environment.

name: Split Anvil
description: When you play a spell, spells in hand that cost less are reduced to 0[ember] for the turn.
lore: After completing the Rail, I destroyed the anvil I used to create all the Railspikes as a symbolic ending to this endeavor.

name: Mind Hoard
description: Increase [emptycorrupt] by [effect0.power] on each floor.
lore: Some use separate bins for organization. Others will place records into random piles and claim the system only lives in their head. Personally, I prefer drawers adorned with precise labels. The Wurmkin use stones with empty slots to keep their Echoes close and contained. What a wonder it is to learn of these civilizations that have developed without our hands to influence...or corrupt.

name: Ancient Pinion
description: When an Angel moves it gains [valor] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power].
lore: The fossil of a great winged beast from which it is said all angels descend from. Question is, what was it doing in the last circle of Hell?

name: Nefarious Overflow
description: [unstable] explosions deal twice as much damage.
lore: I spilled this mixture and let me say, the result was not pleasant. Hugo, assistant to Dr. Orechi

name: Emot Tome
description: Create an [ephemeral] copy of the first spell you play each turn.
lore: A historical account of the great battles between Heaven and Hell before the Covenant. Written in the back is a first hand account from a demon about the first days after the Covenant was broken.

name: Twisting Mycelium
description: On turn start [spawn] [effect0.effect0.status0.power] on each floor per [effect0.power] cards in your Deck.
lore: In moments, the clearing was overrun with the Decay and the bones that housed our children were lifted from the earth to feed the evil. The Archives of the Great Decay

name: Medallion of Superiority
description: Units gain +[effect0.power][health] and +[effect1.power][attack] for each upgrade on their card.
lore: A trinket made of fool's gold given to dragons who have proven supreme aptitude for business.

name: Karmic Censer
description: [shift] triggers an additional time.
lore: Why does this smell like chocolate? asked Fel. What's chocolate? asked Talos.

name: Sap Tap
description: The first time each turn a friendly unit is healed, draw [effect0.power].
lore: Intruders often try to tap the Wildwood to harvest its sap, though the Wildwood usually ends up harvesting the intruders instead. The Edge Priory has allowed me to collect these taps for my own personal research.

name: Broken Rail
description: When you [forge] a unit or equipment, apply +[effect0.power][health] for each [forgepoint] spent.
lore: The Rail is what bound Heaven and the clans of Hell to the Covenant. The act of driving in your spike was the equivalent of signing a contract. The only way for the Covenant to be broken was for the Rail to be broken first, which was not a simple task.Herzal, My Workshop, My Life

name: Molten Manifold
description: [x] Cost cards get +[effect0.power] to their X value when played.
lore: Within the foundry, molten streams flowed constantly within large systems of troughs, each one feeding to various molds for casting. The stewards working the foundry needed no respite, which meant fresh steel was always at the ready.

name: Fade's First Blade
description: Friendly units gain [rage] [effect0.status0.power] whenever they lose a stack of [burnout].
lore: I should no longer be surprised by Fade's unusual nature. Her lack of wax dates her long before the creation of the Waxers and the Wickless, and the wicks atop her head seem to be purely ornamental. Yet the knife she carries and the code that she lives by, or lack thereof, has many similarities to the Remnant of today.

name: Resin Block
description: When a friendly unit dies, apply +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] to that unit.
lore: With each melt and reform comes the development of new resin, giving the Waxer a particular edge they didn't have in their previous life. I've chipped some away to study further once aboard the Boneshaker.

name: Magma Core
description: Your Pyre applies [pyregel] [effect0.power] to enemy units on all floors on [revenge].
lore: It is a rare occurrence but sometimes the lava that flows between the Pyreborne caves will solidify into a mass humming with power.

name: Progress Pacemaker
description: The first time you [mix] each turn, [mix] again.
lore: All my experiments do take a toll on the cardiovascular system of my assistants. This will fix that. from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Carving Corusca
description: When Extract is used, gain [effect0.power][ember] and [effect1.power][corrupt].
lore: Wurmkin learning to master stoneform carving are often given a set of claw covers to practice. This allows them to practice stoneform etchings without a worry of damaging their own claws. Given how sturdy I've seen Wurmkin claws to be, I'd guess this protection is little more than vanity.

name: Heaven's Light
description: +[effect0.power][capacity] on each floor. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].
lore: The coveted Light of Seraph. Those from above worship it as much as we value the Pyre. From what I've seen it's powerful, sure, but it's not as special as they say. That doesn't mean I won't take some if given the chance.

name: Serrated Mandibles
description: When one or more [corrupt] are added to a floor on your turn, apply [corruptpoison] [effect0.status0.power] to a random enemy unit, twice.
lore: Traveling to the Bogs now, one would not be faulted for missing the conflict between the Wurmkin and the Kinhost. In fact, one would even surmise that no conflict exists at all, and in many ways, it doesn't. I suppose the Wurmkin's swift removal of any Kinhost dissent, or small display of sentience for that matter, has squashed any lingering division. Not quite what I'd consider a victory.

name: Unstable Pyresparks
description: Shield Steward and Spear Steward units gain the Boom Ability.
lore: I did not just create the Stewards to aid me. They also contain a hidden defense mechanism that triggers if the Forge is attacked. I hope to never have to use them but, if I must, I am prepared.

name: Burning Feather
description: When a friendly unit dies, Angels on the floor gain [rage] [effect0.power].
lore: I once wore this with pride. Now, I cannot bear to look at it. Finna the Doomed

name: Jackstrips
description: Deal [effect0.power] [piercing] damage whenever an enemy unit moves between floors.
lore: The stairwells of the Boneshaker are never what they seem. Among other surprises, the hidden spike traps I've engineered can be set to stop any combatant.

name: Fhyra's Inferno
description: Dragons apply [pyregel] [effect0.power] on [strike].
lore: A small effigy representing the mighty Fhyra, mother of the Pyreborne and whose rules all dragons must follow.

name: Pyrestone Housing
description: Units get an extra upgrade slot.
lore: My discovery of the creation of Pyrestones, gemstones infused with flames of the Pyre, was monumental in enhancing the strength of Hell's forces and marked a turning point in the war against Heaven. That victory was short-lived, however, as the design was stolen and copied shortly thereafter.

name: Wanderer's Talisman
description: At start of turn, friendly units gain +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and +[effect0.upgrade.bonushp][health] if they are the only friendly unit on the floor.
lore: A token from better times, found in Limbo without its owner.

name: Limbo's Solace
description: Draw +[effect0.power] each turn. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].
lore: One of my crowning achievements. A metal-based compound that can be formed into any shape. I've only been able to create a small batch of it, but a little goes a long way.

name: Wurmtooth
description:
Clan starter cards are [infused].
One card in each draft pack will be [infused].
lore: The Bogwurm is mentioned very casually among the Wurmkin. So much so that I often forgot the beast was a Titan. But it seems that the Bogwurm that gave them life and shelter is so present in their everyday routines, that their eternal devotion to study is reverence enough to the Titan. Even if they do refer to the Bogwurm as that ghastly old worm more than I care to acknowledge.

name: Founding Seal
description: [incant] triggers an additional time.
lore: Tethys and I created this Seal to commemorate the founding of the Stygian Guard and the protection they are sworn to give to their Unnamed Titan.

name: Surgeon's Suture
description: When you equip a friendly unit, restore them to full health.
lore: In just a snip, tuck, and solder, one soldier's limb can be put onto another. from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Seer Orb
description: When applying [spellweakness], apply [effect0.status0.power] more.
lore: I'll keep my moon here until the time is right. Until then, you'll whisper to me, won't you? Lady Ekka

name: Manifold Mirror
description: The first Room card played each battle is applied to all floors.
lore: A mirror that reflects not only who you are but who you wish to be.

name: Boiler Room Mod
description: At the start of battle, apply Boiler Room on the first floor.
lore: Trains don't run on dreams and wishes. Behind every sheet of metal is an intricately engineered piece of work.

name: Circle of Cycles
description: Restore [effect0.power] health to the lowest health friendly unit on [mooncycle].
lore: Oh, Empress Moon, you had one eye but so many faces! Lady Ekka

name: Spotted Spore
description: [funguy] gain +[effect0.power][attack] per [troop] stack.
lore: Although the Underlegion fled their forest hoping to escape the Great Decay, they brought with them a few unwanted spores. One day, they might find a place to grow and I hope to never see that day.

name: Silver Ember
description: +[effect0.power][ember] and +[effect1.power][deploymentember].

name: Melting Spout
description: [tomb] units get +[effect0.power][health] and [burnout] [effect1.upgrade.status0.power].
lore: Only the wealthiest of Waxers can afford the portable melting pot I created to allow on-demand wax guttering. Out of charity, unfortunate Tombs are given a spout by the Reformed so they can survive.

name: The Unbroken Horn
description: Conserve [ember] between turns and [deployphase].
lore: I've never found the final whereabouts of Grrrg, but before his mysterious disappearance, he left his unbroken horn with the Hellhorned, leading me to believe he has succumbed to death.

name: Memorial Fund
description: Gain [effect0.power][coin] when a friendly unit dies.
lore: In a scheme I refused to take part in, Flicker devised a plan to collect funds from Waxers to benefit those who have passed, only to keep them for himself.

name: Pyreforged Solace
description: Draw +[effect0.power] each turn. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].

name: Limbo's Solace
description: Draw +[effect0.power] each turn. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].
lore: One of my crowning achievements. A metal-based compound that can be formed into any shape. I've only been able to create a small batch of it, but a little goes a long way.

name: Fused Pyreshard
description: When your Pyre defeats an enemy, it permanently gains +[effect0.power] [attack].
lore: The day I defied the Child, I bound their essence within a Shardsoul. But the vessel I prepared could not hold. The Shardsoul fractured into several distinct shards, each with their own unique properties. The Pyre was merely one of those shards. And now that I see the Pyre's own fragments can be fused back together, I cannot dismiss the possibility that the Shardsoul itself could be restored. Should that ever occur, I fear the result will be catastrophic.Herzal, My Workshop, My Life

name: Cursed Vines
description: At start of turn, add a Vine Grasp spell with [ephemeral] to your hand.
lore: Not all of the Edge Priory endeavors have been successes. Their attempts to return to the physical form of an Animus have been met with countless failures. The vines they've used in these experiments wither with the unstable energy that's cursed them.

name: Contingency Plans
description: Monstrosities enter with [spikes] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: The effects of grafting body parts to creatures of opposite demonic species often results in surprising abilities. from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Abandoned Antumbra
description: At start of turn, add a common or uncommon [snack] unit to hand.
lore: I found this Morsel abandoned in the mines of the Crucible with all of its appendages missing. It seems to have taken a liking to me.

name: Guild Marker
description: Merchant costs are reduced by [effect0.power]%.
lore: Despite my several attempts to win the support of the furry traders, the merchants of Hell have decided to stay neutral. Finally, after much pestering, they allowed me into their guild. That hasn't stopped them from wringing me of any spare coin.

name: Fhyra's Breath
description: Whelps apply [pyregel] [effect0.power] on [strike].
lore: Visitors of Fhyra's temple can buy cute charms at the gift shop. This one costs three gold coins.

name: Ashes of the Fallen
description: [summon] triggers an additional time.
lore: According to the Hellhorned, the dead are never really gone. Their remains are cremated and used as warpaint to imbue warriors with great strength and remind them of their eventual return to the ground.

name: Pyreforged Flame
description: +[effect0.power][ember] per turn. +[effect3.power][deploymentember]. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].

name: Part Factory
description: On [deployphase], add a random [graft] unit to your hand.
lore: The craftsman approach is no more! Time to use an assembly line to create my monsters. from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Shadowbox
description: When you play your 20th [snack] unit of the battle, deal [effect0.power] damage to enemy units on all floors.
lore: Supposedly, these crystal Shardsouls once contained sacrificed souls and were created by the Exiles in a gambit to save Heaven, Hell, and Human. Now empty, the crystal's remains house many Morsels. This may confirm my theory that the Umbra Shroud is made of pure soul.

name: Kinstone Totem
description: When a card is discarded before the end of your turn, gain [effect0.power][ember].
lore: For as long as I've lived in Hell, I've known the Ring filled with Bogwurm remains to be a desolate place with no sentient inhabitants. When Solgard mentioned a Kinstone gifted to him by a clan that resides there, the Wurmkin, I realized there's so much I still don't know about this place. Or, perhaps, I can no longer remember.

name: Decayed Decoy
description: Grant +[effect0.status0.power] stack of [corruptpoison] each time it is applied.
lore: I like to think that, over time, I've become more empathetic to decisions made that I may not make myself. The Spine Chief's decision to keep the Wurmkin hidden for all these years is one of those decisions  one I would not make, but I understand. Empathy, however, does not require respect.

name: Totem Fragment
description: Apply [spellweakness] [effect0.status0.power] to enemy units when they enter the floor below the Pyre Room.
lore: From my studies of the Stygian totems, I've found that the sidestones that circle around them help to focus their energy. When removed from their totem host, these sidestones can produce a similar, though much weaker, effect on their target.

name: Thornfruit
description: At start of turn, add a Sting spell to your hand.
lore: After a thorn has lodged into the ground and released its spores, it will wilt and return to the Wildwood. On very rare occasions, the thorn will produce a fruit that is coveted among Channelers, though I find it personally much too sour.

name: Catalyzing Agent
description: At end of turn, [unstable] increases by [effect1.power].
lore: I'm not sure what it does except that it does have a wonderful and fresh minty flavor. from Dr. Orechi's notebook

name: Spell Sanctum Mod
description: At the start of battle, apply Spell Sanctum on the second floor.
lore: With her father's Boneshaker, Heph didn't want to change any of the original designs. But with her own trains, she was willing to build wherever her imagination took her.

name: The Bloating Fungus
description: [regen] restores +[effect0.power] health per stack.
lore: This fungal infection affects the bark of trees throughout the Wildwood. While it feeds on much of the sap the tree produces, the fungus also accelerates the tree's sap production entirely, creating a fascinating symbiotic relationship between the two species.

name: Cavendish
description: Non-champion friendly units gain [effect0.secondarypower]x base [attack]. At the end of combat on all floors, [effect1.power]% chance for this artifact to be destroyed.
lore: That other banana wasn't very a-peel-ing, was it?

name: Kwilling Catcher
description: At the end of battle, gain [effect0.trigger0.effect0.power][coin].
lore: A nifty net with traces of gold-lit orbs gathered inside. They'd probably fetch a pretty penny.

name: Ancient Roots
description: The first spell played each turn has -1[ember] for every [effect0.power] cards in your Deck.
lore: The roots of the Fatal Elm carve through the sand of Limbo, through the earth of Hell, past each circle until they reach the Ninth Forbidden Realm, and continue past into a world unknown to any being.

name: A Forgotten Name
description: When you play your third spell of the turn, all cards gain +[effect0.power] [magicpower] for the rest of this battle.
lore: When we imprisoned the Titan for the safety of Hell, the Stygian Guard stripped it of its name. When the Titan is released again, its name will return with it.

name: Cortical Connector
description: [shroom] units gain [regen] [effect0.power] on [harvest].
lore: The fungus that grows along the roots of the Fatal Elm is in fact one single neural network that consumes bodies and uses them for its own mysterious purpose.

name: Cleansing Water
description: [effect0.power]% chance to remove all [buff] effects on an enemy unit when it enters your train.
lore: During my time in Heaven, I was gifted some of their purifying water, but the liquid was so strong that it would burn anything it touched. So, I put it aside. It has now found a new use as a repellant in the Boneshaker.

name: Pyreforged Light
description: +[effect0.power][capacity] on each floor. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].

name: Ancient Pyretap
description: When you are out of [ember], cards can be played for their cost in Pyre Health.
lore: The Pyreborne, always looking to exact more than what can be given, found a gruesome method to collect Pyre magic: plunging a stake in the outer shell and installing a tap.

name: Heaven's Light
description: +[effect0.power][capacity] on each floor. [halfbreak]Your Pyre gets +[effect2.pyreattackpower][attack] and +[effect1.pyrehealthpower][pyrehealth].
lore: The coveted Light of Seraph. Those from above worship it as much as we value the Pyre. From what I've seen it's powerful, sure, but it's not as special as they say. That doesn't mean I won't take some if given the chance.

name: Martyr's Signet
description: At the end of battle, the front friendly unit on each floor permanently gains +[effect0.trigger0.effect0.upgrade.charactertrigger0.effect0.upgrade.bonushp][health].
lore: A ring that belonged to Finna the Doomed. May it bring greater luck to whoever now wears it.

name: Odi's Totem
description: +[effect1.power][ember] per turn. [effect0.power][deploymentember].
lore: This statuette has the uncanny ability of following its owner with its eyes wherever they go.

name: Mold Braces
description: Friendly units apply [armor] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power] to the front friendly unit on [extinguish].
lore: Not all who enter the mold do so willingly. The need for restraints, while I consider it cruel, has been effective in solidifying these 'participants' will to reform or, sometimes, to melt for the sake of others.

name: Rules of Containment
description: Enemy units enter with [frostbite] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: These ancient scrolls detail the laws of the Guard, from ceremonial offerings to mundane dress codes. They are a historical treasure trove that I look forward to studying more when this whole affair is finished.

name: Silent Sigil
description: When it becomes [new], apply [armor] [effect0.status0.power] to friendly Silent units.
lore: A banner torn from the ancient temple of the Luna Coven. The fae hope that one day they can hang this cloth once more.

name: Lunar Lantern
description: Selene units get +[effect1.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] during [fullmoon]. Silent units get +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] during [newmoon].
lore: A lantern that illuminates depending on the phase of the moon.

name: Unstable Shard
description: Friendly units get +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage][attack] and +[effect0.upgrade.bonushp][health].
lore: When the Last Divinity died, the divine shards scattered across all of Heaven and Hell. Fragments of those shards still remain, cackling with latent divine energy.

name: Nim's Oath
description: At start of turn, apply [dazed] [effect0.effect0.status0.power] to the front enemy unit on a random floor.
lore: These shattered orbs were called 'Bindings' and still contains a trace of its power. One thing is for certain, this item is not of this world.

name: Judge's Scales
description: On [deployphase], discard any number of cards, then draw that many.
lore: Some readers may see Herzal's tale as one of strength and judgment. However a careful editor reveals a different truth: a story of regret and sorrow, ending with the loss of hisand everyone else'smemories. The past, however, has a way of catching up with us.The Historian

name: Flaming Talons
description: When an enemy unit ascends, they gain [pyregel] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: Said to be the talons of Fhyra herself, cut from her body during the first battle between Titans that ended with the first Pyre's destruction.

name: Shadow's Sheath
description: Friendly units gain [stealth] [effect1.power] on [summon] and [slay]. +[effect0.power][attack] per stack of [stealth].
lore: They say Death himself walks beside the rail, and that is not a figure of speech. Though none have said it for long.

name: Purified Soul Shard
description: Unit cards without upgrades cost [effect0.power][ember].
lore: What happens to the souls trapped within soul shards? No one is sure. There are cases of shards becoming 'purified', a transformation denoted by a change in color.

name: Fight Club Mod
description: At the start of battle, apply Fight Club on the third floor.
lore: The first trains weren't built for warfare, they were meant to connect the people of Heaven and Hell together. But now, the trains have been fully outfitted as war machines.

name: Verdant Cycle
description: The first time each turn a spell card with [consume] is played, draw [effect0.power].
lore: Where the branches of the Fatal Elm reach beyond Heaven, a spore grows anew. Maybe this is a sign that this tree will become the Creation Elm once again.

name: Echo Seedling
description: The first time each battle a card with [consume] is played, add [effect0.power] copies to hand.
lore: One more recent Wurmkin experiment has been to propagate an Echo's stored knowledge. This involves taking a small shard of a source and placing it into a shallow plate of water. Some amount of knowledge is maintained in the newly formed crystal, but not yet enough to make the process widely adopted.

name: Celestial Cascade
description: When a friendly unit gains [valor], it gains +[effect0.status0.power] stacks.
lore: When I fled Heaven, I did not leave empty handed, said Talos. She overturned the jar. Fel gasped. Celestial gems, each containing enough power to smite an army, tumbled onto the table.

name: Chicot
description: Bosses start with [mute] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: I am craven, and thou art my master.

name: Expanded Coffers
description: Increase max [dragonshoardicon] by [effect0.power].
lore: You can learn a lot about a dragon by how much gold is in their coffers. old Pyreborne adage

name: Pyreborne's Insignia
description: When you equip a friendly unit, apply [conduit] [effect0.power].
lore: Clients will always remember a great logo. The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #98

name: Grrrg's Goad
description: [demon] units get [multistrike] [effect0.upgrade.status0.power].
lore: Though credited with building the Hellhorned's section of the Rail, Grrrg wasn't able to complete it without help from other demons. Some needed more motivation than others.

name: Twin Minds
description: Create a permanent copy of the first [consume] card played each battle.
lore: The two moved in unison, as if pulled by the invisible hands of a puppet master. Problem was, the two soldiers had long died on the battlefield. The Archives of the Great Decay

name: Silver Capacity
description: +[effect0.power][capacity].

name: Hellheart
description: Apply [pyregel] [effect0.status0.power] to Non-Flying Boss enemy units that enter the floor below the Pyre Room.
lore: Before the Pyreborne became the greedy dragons they are now, they would channel their passions into rubies they wore around their necks.

name: Radiant Arms
description: When you equip a friendly unit, apply [damageshield] [effect0.trigger0.effect0.status0.power].
lore: Can you make it match my wings? I have to think about my brand. Talos

name: Shadelamp
description: The first time each turn an enemy unit dies, add [effect0.power] [snack] units to hand.
lore: When the Rail was built, the Crucible became accessible to Hellborne other than the Umbra Shroud. The Shroud was not too welcoming, however, and crafted lights of shadow that only they could use to see, making it impossible for tourists to linger.

name: Artificial Pyrestone
description: +[effect0.power][deploymentember].
lore: A trinket created to give a burst of Ember, unfortunately too unstable and expensive to be manufactured in bulk.

name: Blank Pages
description: At start of turn, if you do not have a Champion in your hand, add a random one to your hand.
lore: Times are changing. Divinities are making rules while we keep trying to save our own skins. Well, not anymore. There's more souls out there who can help us, there's got to be. And it's about time someone set out to find them. So, I guess, this is where I'll try and record that search. I'll bet old Herzal's turning in his ice at the thought. Don't worry, I fail like the best of 'em.

name: Yorick
description: When a card with [consume] is played, gain [effect0.power][coin].
lore: Alas, poor Yorick! I knew him, Horatio; a fellow of infinite jest.

name: Hardened Hull
description: When an Egg unit is summoned, remove [effect0.status0.power] [hatch] and apply [armor] [effect1.status0.power].
lore: Eggs are rarely hatched as soon as they are created. In fact, new eggs have not been laid for centuries. So the dormant eggs are incubated in calcified Kinhost carapace. Though, if no new eggs exist, I suspect that the Wurmkin's sudden announcement of their existence is less selfless than they'd have me believe.

name: Scorched Steel
description: Friendly units enter with [armor] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: Steel hammered in the heat of the Scorched Plains is easily recognized by its banding. After the freeze, the steel became in short supply, but I've still been able to stockpile a small amount for defensive enhancements.

name: Historian's Razor
description: Friendly units get +[effect1.power][attack] but [effect0.power][attack] for every non-boss and non-starter Artifact you own.
lore: The recording of history can be much more speculative than one might think, for even the most objective historians. When it is up to a historian's imagination, the simplest explanations are the most likely to have occurred.

name: Golden Gloves
description: Friendly units gain [avarice] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: A gift for my shining dumpling after she kicked me out of our cave. I hope she likes the gloves. Or else she will not let me come home. Lord Fenix

name: Notice Stone
description: When a card with [consume] is played, all cards gain +[effect0.power] [magicpower] for the rest of this battle.
lore: Wurmkin do not sleep. Underground, day and night are merely talked about in the academic sense. As such, Wurmkin will study for days, sometimes weeks, without interruption, so direct contact between Wurmkin is rare. Instead, the Wurmkin use open stone walls as notice boards.

name: Railhammer
description: When a friendly unit gains [armor], it gains +[effect0.status0.power] stacks.
lore: Railhammers have been forged in the deep pits of the Scorched Plains since the founding of our Covenant, making them durable tools in the construction of Hellhorned armor.

name: Golden Idol
description: Trial [coin] rewards are increased by [effect0.power]%.
lore: A shining visage of the Titan of Savagery. Some wish to see it melted for scrap while others advocate turning it against its progenitor.

name: Ember Charge
description: On your first turn, +[effect0.power][ember].
lore: Although an ember won't be able to offer much energy, it's enough to spark a keg of Pyregel or two.

name: Stardust Treat
description: The first unit you summon each turn gains [conduit] [effect0.status0.power].
lore: A tasty treat made of stardust, the coven love to take a pause when the moon is half full and eat these with tea.

name: Capricious Reflection
description: Cards in reward packs and unit banners come with a random upgrade.
lore: Waters touched by fragments of the lost Divinities show us reflections of another world. A world where the Divine Mother governed over the creation of life and the responsibility of death. Given the purview of her powers, it follows that her destruction created the many immortal beings of Heaven and Hell and led to our current predicament.

name: Bog Slime
description: When a spell with [consume] is played, gain [effect0.power][corrupt].
lore: The bogs and decay on the Ring's topside acts as a sort of camouflage for those within and a deterrent from anyone wanting to investigate further. I've seen bodies decomposed in minutes on more than one occasion. So, I wouldn't say I was excited to return to the bogs for any reason.

name: Tethys' Scales
description: [effect0.power]% chance to apply [spellweakness] [effect0.effect0.status0.power] when an enemy unit enters your train.
lore: As a symbolic sacrifice to convince her fellow sea dwellers of her commitment to the Covenant and the confinement of the Titan, Tethys removed her own scales. I don't understand their ways, but the gesture worked as she intended.

name: Pyre Piping
description: While the Pyre is at full health, draw +[effect0.power] each turn.
lore: While the Pyre itself is magical, the means of which it powers the train is through pure engineering. These pipes were designed to absorb and transfer the Pyre's heat into several boilers. From there, that heat is converted to mechanical energy through the piston rods, generating power that drives the locomotive.

name: Waxer Snuffer
description: [extinguish] triggers an additional time.
lore: For the less committed Wickless enthusiasts who are unwilling to remove their wick entirely, the snuffer provides a glimpse into a possible wick-free life. I've helped some Waxers dim their flames, though most prefer to do it themselves.

name: Lifemother's Bloom
description: At the end of combat, create a permanent copy of a non-champion card in your deck.
lore: The Lifemother is often linked to the Wildwood, but in truth, She shaped all living things...for it was She who bound soul to vessel. A vessel without a soul is an empty husk; a soul without a vessel is mere shadow. Only in their union does life arise.The Historian

name: Thorn Casing
description: Sting spells get +[effect0.upgrade.bonusdamage] [magicpower] and [piercing].
lore: Using the smithing techniques I taught them, the Edge Priory developed casings for the thorns ejected from the Awoken, turning them into much deadlier weapons against the Winged.
